citation.authors: Nelson DA, Deuster PA, Carter R, Hill OT et al

cited_by.title: Sickle cell trait and hard exercise

record.population: 47,944 Black US Army soldiers tested for sickle cell trait (HbAS), 2011-2014
record.design: Cohort study with Cox models, adjusted for known risk factors, among soldiers under exertional-injury precautions
record.finding: No significant difference in death risk between soldiers with and without the trait (hazard ratio 0.99, 95% CI 0.46-2.13). Exertional rhabdomyolysis risk was higher with the trait (adjusted HR 1.54, 95% CI 1.12-2.12), similar in size to the effect of tobacco use (HR 1.54) and of a BMI of 30 or more (HR 1.39).
record.note: Soldiers were already under exertional-injury precautions, so this tells you about risk when precautions are in place, not without them.
